channel.title: KhingShot
channel.description: Update feed for KhingShot, the macOS capture app.

item.description:
KhingShot 0.3.1

Fixes Check for Updates…, which could find a new version and then fail to offer it.

  • Choosing Check for Updates… from the menu bar or Check Now in Settings could leave the update panel unshown, with no message either way, and the item disabled until the app was relaunched. Both now bring up the update panel as soon as a newer version is found.
  • When there is nothing to install, the check still answers with a toast rather than a modal, and the menu item always becomes clickable again once the check finishes.
  • Automatic background checks were never affected and are unchanged, as is everything in capture, recording, annotation, and the library.

If Check for Updates… is greyed out on 0.3.0, quitting and relaunching KhingShot clears it. Updating to this version stops it happening again.

Requires macOS 14.0 or later.

KhingShot 0.3.0

Navigating and fixing up a markup now works the way it does in every design tool you already use.

Zoom and pan the canvas

  • Hold Command and scroll to zoom. Zooming happens around the pointer, so the spot you are pointing at stays put instead of sliding off screen. A mouse wheel and a trackpad each get their own feel, and one hard flick can no longer throw you across the whole range.
  • Hold Space and drag to pan, with the open and closed hand cursor. The pan never draws, selects, or nudges an annotation by accident, and Space still types a space while you are editing a text box.
  • Zoom runs from 10% to 800%, and the zoom buttons now stop at the same limits.
  • Let go of Space, switch apps, or Command-Tab away, and the hand tool releases with it. The canvas cannot get stuck in pan mode.

Reshape arrows after you draw them

  • Select an arrow or a line with the Select tool and each end gets a grip. Drag one to move that end while the other stays anchored. Aim or length slightly off no longer means deleting it and drawing it again.
  • Works on straight pen and highlighter strokes too, the ones made by holding Shift while drawing. Freehand strokes are unchanged.

Requires macOS 14.0 or later.

KhingShot 0.2.1

A verification cut. Same features as 0.2.0, published so that the update path introduced in that release could be exercised end to end: an installed 0.2.0 finds this version in the feed, installs it, and relaunches on its own.

  • Confirms the full chain works on a real machine: appcast fetch, EdDSA

signature check, download, in-place swap in /Applications, and relaunch, with no Gatekeeper prompt at any point.

  • No functional changes to capture, recording, annotation, or the library.

Requires macOS 14.0 or later.

KhingShot 0.2.0

The first release that can update itself. Earlier builds had no way to learn that a new version had shipped, so every update meant downloading a DMG by hand.

Automatic updates

  • KhingShot now checks for a new version once a day in the background. When one

is available you get the standard macOS update panel with release notes and Install Update, Skip This Version, and Remind Me Later.

  • Updates install and relaunch on their own once you approve them.
  • A background check that finds nothing shows no UI at all, and no update prompt

will interrupt you while a capture or recording is in progress.

New controls

  • Check for Updates… in the menu bar dropdown, next to About and Settings.
  • Settings → General → Updates shows the current version, an

Automatically check for updates switch (on by default), a Check Now button, and when the last check ran.

Under the hood

  • Updates are delivered by Sparkle 2, the

standard macOS update framework, and are the first third-party dependency in the app.

  • Every download is signed twice over: a Developer ID signature notarized by

Apple, plus an EdDSA signature that KhingShot verifies before it installs anything.

  • Version numbers now move with each release, so the updater has something real

to compare. This build reports 0.2.0 where every earlier cut reported 0.1.0.

Requires macOS 14.0 or later.
